tasks.title: Add cron-parser dependency and schedule-parser utility
tasks.description: Add `cron-parser` to package.json dependencies. Create `src/services/schedule-parser.ts` with a `parseDuration()` function that converts duration strings ("30m", "24h", "1d", "45s") to milliseconds, and a `computeNextRun()` function that takes a parsed schedule config ({ every, cron, at, anchor }) and returns the next run timestamp as an ISO string. Also add a `parseScheduleConfig()` function that validates and normalizes the raw schedule object from SKILL.md frontmatter into a typed ScheduleConfig.
acceptanceCriteria: parseDuration('30m') returns 1800000
parseDuration('24h') returns 86400000
parseDuration('1d') returns 86400000
parseDuration('abc') throws or returns null
computeNextRun for { every: '5m' } returns a future timestamp ~5 minutes from now
computeNextRun for { cron: '0 9 * * 1-5' } returns next weekday 09:00
computeNextRun for { at: '2026-05-01T10:00:00Z' } returns that exact timestamp
computeNextRun for { every: '24h', anchor: '09:00' } returns next 09:00
parseScheduleConfig rejects invalid configs and returns null
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: No dependency on #99 skill infrastructure — pure utility functions. This is the foundation all other tasks build on.

Export ScheduleRepo from `src/db/index.ts` and add getter to StateManager.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration v16 runs without errors on fresh and existing DB (v15)
agent_skill_schedules table has all required columns

ScheduleRepo.getAllEnabled returns only enabled schedules
ScheduleRepo.deleteBySkillId removes schedule row
ScheduleRepo exported from db/index.ts

tasks.title: Implement SchedulerService core
tasks.description: Create `src/services/scheduler-service.ts` with SchedulerService class. Constructor takes ScheduleRepo, SkillService (from #99), and EventBus. Methods: start() loads enabled schedules and arms timers; stop() clears all timers; armTimer(schedule) sets a setTimeout clamped to max 60s delay; onTimerFire(schedule) executes the skill via SkillService.runSkill(), updates next_run_at in DB, re-arms timer; handleOneShot(schedule) executes and disables the schedule. On execution failure, log the error but still compute and schedule next run. Emit schedule_triggered / schedule_completed / schedule_failed events via EventBus. Concurrent executions respect maxConcurrentRuns — excess schedules are queued and run when a slot opens.
acceptanceCriteria: SchedulerService.start() loads enabled schedules from DB and arms timers
Timer fires invoke SkillService.runSkill() with the skill name
After fire, next_run_at is recomputed and persisted to DB
After fire, a new timer is armed for the new next_run_at
One-shot (at) schedules are disabled after firing (enabled=0)
Execution failure is logged but next_run_at still computed and timer re-armed
Timer delays are clamped to max 60 seconds (re-check pattern)
SchedulerService.stop() clears all active timers
EventBus events emitted: schedule_triggered, schedule_completed, schedule_failed
When multiple schedules fire simultaneously, they respect maxConcurrentRuns limit
Excess concurrent schedules are queued and executed when a slot opens
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Depends on T-001 for schedule-parser (computeNextRun) and T-003 for ScheduleRepo. Also depends on #99's SkillService existing.

tasks.title: Implement restart recovery in SchedulerService
tasks.description: Add `recover()` method to SchedulerService. On start, after loading enabled schedules, check each schedule's next_run_at. If next_run_at is in the past, trigger one immediate catch-up execution for that schedule, then compute new next_run_at from now. For 'at' schedules that are past, execute once and disable. At most one catch-up per schedule regardless of how far in the past next_run_at is.
acceptanceCriteria: Recovery loads all enabled schedules and checks next_run_at vs now
Overdue schedules trigger exactly one catch-up execution immediately
After catch-up, next_run_at is computed from now (not from missed time)
Schedules with future next_run_at are armed normally without catch-up
Overdue 'at' schedules execute once then are disabled (enabled=0)
If schedule was overdue by days, only one execution fires (not multiple)
Typecheck passes

SSE handler registers listeners for the new event types
